findings_assessed.finding_text: 98.3% CDM cascade leakage across three layers (1,000 NCD-eligible patients funnel to ~17 in controlled CDM management), with Layer 2 anchored at 77.4% leakage from PMC 12021225.

counter_evidence.implication: PMC 12021225 is a South Korean Samsung Electronics study (2013-2016, onsite clinic). Used as Malaysia/Indonesia proxy without geographic disclosure. The 77.4% Layer 2 anchor has no validated SEA corporate MCU analogue in public literature.

Lancet GBD 2025 global cascade reports 21% of all diabetics globally in optimal management — directionally consistent with the corpus endpoint but uses general-population framing, not serial corporate-MCU-to-TPA path.

counter_cases_ignored: HealthMetrics-integrated MY corporate MCU may have materially different follow-up rates than 22.6% South Korean figure
Prolanis 56.8% dropout (Layer 3) is East Java public sector — private TPA dynamics may differ
Cascade serially multiplies leakage rates across non-overlapping cohorts
findings_assessed.suggested_deep_research_question: Search PubMed for any published Malaysia/Indonesia corporate MCU post-screening CDM follow-up rate; if none exists, flag as primary-data gap requiring HealthMetrics or SOCSO field interview.

findings_assessed.finding_text: 67% of MY specialists report GL revocation post-admission (CodeBlue Oct 2025 survey, n=855); anchors sub-step 3a as 3rd highest cost concentration and drives MY Layer 3 pilot rationale.

counter_evidence.implication: Insurance industry response (90%+ approval rate) uses different denominator; no audited BNM/TPA GL revocation rate published.
CodeBlue survey used convenience sampling via medical association networks distributing survey framed as investigating insurance problems — textbook volunteer/selection bias.

counter_cases_ignored: 67% figure not decomposed by revocation legitimacy (some may be appropriate policy application)
Faster-SLA insurers (Generali 1-hr, Allianz 45-min) suggest 6-hr average is upper-bound not median
BNM Dec 2025 directive + MOF statements indicate active regulatory reform may shift the problem before 2026
findings_assessed.suggested_deep_research_question: Search BNM Financial Stability Review / LIAM for any audited GL denial rate; relabel 67% as 'specialist perception rate (convenience sample)' and downgrade from High to Medium confidence.

findings_assessed.finding_text: Malaysia Layer 2 sub-step 2d (post-MCU CDM routing via HealthMetrics) is the recommended fastest path to pilot (Stage 5 §5.4 primary recommendation).

counter_evidence.implication: 22.6% Layer 2 leakage anchor is from 2013-2016 South Korean Samsung onsite clinic — 8-12 years old, structurally distinct setting, no MY/ID equivalent published.
SOCSO SEHATi portal may already provide government-mandated CDM referral pathway for HSP-enrolled employers, narrowing addressable market for a third-party AI product.

counter_cases_ignored: Indonesia Layer 2 via Prodia sub-step 2c (LIS-to-PDF auto-generation) has fewer open assumptions and no geographic misattribution — may be more evidence-robust
HealthMetrics itself may build sub-step 2d (becoming a competitor, not partner)
Stage 5 readiness matrix scores are unweighted averages; uncertainty-weighted ranking could shift the layer/market choice
findings_assessed.suggested_deep_research_question: (1) Confirm HealthMetrics' current sub-step 2d automation status via product documentation + direct inquiry. (2) Confirm whether SOCSO SEHATi includes post-screening CDM referral workflow for HSP-enrolled employers.

summary.most_impactful_gap: F1 and F3 share root cause: PMC 12021225 (22.6% post-MCU CDM follow-up) is South Korean Samsung Electronics, applied as Malaysia/Indonesia proxy without geographic qualification. This single misattribution simultaneously unanchors the WH5 cascade's Layer 2 step (98.3% leakage figure) AND removes quantitative foundation for the primary pilot recommendation. Resolution requires Malaysia/Indonesia-specific corporate MCU post-screening CDM follow-up rate — likely a primary-data gap requiring field validation.
